AWS Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) is a virtual network dedicated to an AWS account.
It provides a logically isolated section of the AWS Cloud where you can launch AWS resources such as Amazon EC2 instances, Elastic Load Balancers, and RDS databases.
Main Features of AWS VPC:.
IP Address Range Configuration: You can select and configure the IP address range for your VPC, typically using an IPv4 CIDR block (e.g., 10.0.0.0/16)..
Subnet Creation: Within a VPC, you can create one or more subnets, each with its own IP address range and associated Availability Zones..
Route Tables and Network Gateways: You can configure route tables to define how network traffic is routed within the VPC and attach internet gateways or virtual private gateways for VPN connections..
Security Settings: Security groups and network access control lists (ACLs) can be applied to control inbound and outbound traffic at the instance and subnet levels..

Default VPC Provisioning: When you create an AWS account, a default VPC is automatically provisioned in each Region, pre-configured with subnets in each Availability Zone, an internet gateway, and a main route table that routes traffic to the internet..
Internet Access for Instances: Instances launched in subnets of a default VPC have automatic access to the internet due to the attached internet gateway and configured route tables..
Dedicated Instances Support: VPCs support launching Dedicated Instances, which run in a tenancy isolated environment for enhanced security and compliance..

Flow Logs for Monitoring: You can create VPC Flow Logs to capture network traffic information, including EFA (Elastic Fabric Adapter) traffic, and publish logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs or S3 for monitoring and analysis..

Comparison of AWS Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) and Amazon Elastic Container Service (ECS)  

---

### **1.

Core Purpose

| Feature | AWS VPC | Amazon ECS |
|---|---|---|
| Primary Function** | Provides a logically isolated section of the AWS cloud where you can launch AWS resources such as EC2 instances, RDS databases, etc., with control over IP address ranges, subnets, and network gateways.
| Manages containerized applications across AWS Regions in the cloud and on‑premises without requiring you to manage the underlying infrastructure (servers, nodes).

|
| Use Case Focus | Network isolation and connectivity for any AWS resources.
| Container orchestration and deployment of microservices or batch jobs using containers.

| *Source: [AWS > EC2 > Virtual private clouds](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/welcome.html) & [AWS > ECS > What is Amazon Elastic Container Service?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ecs/latest/userguide/what-is-amazon-ecs.html)* --- ### **2.

Key Features

#### AWS VPC**.
IP Address Management: Define CIDR blocks, create subnets, and manage IP address allocation..
Network Gateways & Connectivity: Connect to the internet (IGW), connect to your data center via VPN or Direct Connect, and route traffic between subnets using route tables..
Security Controls: Configure security groups (firewall rules) and network ACLs for inbound/outbound traffic filtering..
Isolation: Each VPC is isolated from other VPCs; you can have multiple VPCs within the same account/region..
*Source: [AWS > EC2 > Virtual private clouds](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Introduction.html)* #### Amazon ECS.
Serverless Compute with AWS Fargate: Run containers without managing servers; pay only for the compute resources you use..
External Instances (ECS Anywhere): Manage on‑premises container workloads using the same ECS console and CLI, extending cloud orchestration to hybrid environments..
EC2 Launch Type: Full control over EC2 instances where you manage capacity planning and node maintenance..
Integration with AWS Services: Amazon ECR: Store and pull Docker images securely..
Integration with AWS Services: CloudWatch Logs & Metrics: Monitor container logs, performance metrics, and set alarms..
Integration with AWS Services: IAM Permissions: Fine‑grained access control per container for security isolation..
Service Discovery: Automatically register containers with AWS Cloud Map for easy service location within microservice architectures..

*Source: [AWS > ECS > What is Amazon Elastic Container Service?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ecs/latest/userguide/welcome.html) & [AWS > ECS > Common use cases in Amazon ECS > Additional resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ecs/latest/userguide/common-use-cases.html)* --- ### **3.

Use Cases

| Scenario | AWS VPC | Amazon ECS |
|---|---|---|
| Isolated Network for EC2, RDS, ELB** | Ideal for launching any compute resources (EC2, RDS, Lambda via VPC endpoints) in a secure, isolated network environment.
| Not applicable; focuses on container orchestration rather than raw instance networking.

|
| Hybrid Cloud Container Management | Can be used to connect on‑premises data centers to AWS via VPN/Direct Connect for overall network traffic.
| ECS Anywhere specifically enables managing containers both in the cloud and on‑premises, leveraging VPC connectivity under the hood.

|
| Microservices with Automatic Service Discovery | Requires additional tools (e.g., AWS Cloud Map) or custom implementations; not a native feature of VPC.
| Provides built‑in service discovery via AWS Cloud Map integration, simplifying microservice communication.

|
| Serverless Container Execution | Not directly related; VPC is infrastructure for any compute type.
| Fargate offers serverless container execution without node management.

|
| Custom Network Topology & Security Policies | Highly customizable with subnets, route tables, security groups, and network ACLs.
| Uses VPC networking under the hood when deploying ECS tasks/services; inherits VPC security policies but abstracts many details for containers.

Global Distribution: Azure Cosmos DB allows elastic scaling of throughput and storage across any number of geographical regions, ensuring low-latency access to data worldwide..

Low Latency: Utilizing SSD-backed storage, Azure Cosmos DB delivers order-of-millisecond response times..

Flexible Consistency Levels: It supports multiple consistency levels (eventual, consistent prefix, session, bounded staleness) to balance performance and data freshness according to application needs..
Cost-Effective Pricing Model: Storage and throughput are metered independently, allowing for a flexible pricing model that adapts to usage patterns..
Reserved Throughput: Enables planning in terms of reads/writes rather than underlying hardware resources like CPU or memory..
Scalability: Designed to handle massive request volumes, supporting trillions of requests per day..
These attributes make Azure Cosmos DB well-suited for high-performance applications such as web, mobile, gaming, and IoT that require rapid scaling and global reach.

Definition and Cause:.

A cold start is the added latency that occurs when the function app scales from zero instances to one instance after being idle for a few minutes, as the platform scales down to zero instances when no functions are running ()..
The number of dependencies required by the function app can affect the cold start time ()..
Cold start is noted as being more of an issue for synchronous operations, such as HTTP triggers that must return a response ()..

Mitigation Strategies (Plans other than Consumption):
If cold starts are impacting functions, the following plans are recommended to mitigate or eliminate them:.
Premium plan: Supports both prewarmed instances and always ready instances, maintaining a minimum of one instance ()..
Flex Consumption plan: Supports an optional number of always ready instances, which can be defined on a per instance scaling basis.

When purchasing Reserved Instances, the discount applied depends on how the purchase crosses the discount pricing tiers.
There are four possible scenarios:.
No discount: The purchase within a Region remains below the discount threshold ..
Partial discount: The purchase crosses the threshold of the first discount tier.
In this case, the discounted rate is applied to the remaining reservations, while some reservations may not receive a discount ..
Full discount: The entire purchase within a Region falls within one discount tier and is discounted appropriately ..
Two discount rates: The purchase crosses from a lower discount tier to a higher discount tier.
You are charged two different rates: one or more reservations at the lower discounted rate, and the remaining reservations at the higher discounted rate ..
If a purchase crosses into a discounted pricing tier, the service generates multiple Reserved Instance IDs, as there is an ID for each set of reservations in a tier .

GCP offers four provisioning models for Compute Engine instances: Standard, Spot, Flex-start, and Reservation-bound .
Standard (Default): You can create compute instances immediately based on resource availability.
You control when to stop or delete the instances, but Google Cloud may also stop or delete them at any time to reclaim capacity ..
Spot: This model allows you to create compute instances based on resource availability and control when to stop or delete them.
Flex-start: With this model, you can create compute instances within a specified waiting time (up to two hours for standalone Flex-start VM and indefinite for MIG resize request).
You control when to stop or delete the instances, but they run for a minimum of 10 minutes and up to a maximum of seven days ..
Reservation-bound: This model allows you to reserve capacity at a future date for creating compute instances.
During the reservation period, you can stop, restart, delete, and recreate compute instances as needed.
When the reservation period ends, Google Cloud deletes the reservation and stops or deletes any compute instances that consume the reservation based on their termination action ..
They are used to create, update, and delete resources in a consistent and repeatable manner across multiple accounts and regions.

On the other hand, managing your own database on an Amazon EC2 instance gives you full control over the database, but it requires more effort in terms of management tasks such as patching, backups, and scaling.

Across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Availability Zones (AZs) are unique physical locations within a cloud provider's region that provide increased fault tolerance and resiliency.
Definition: AWS : Availability Zones are multiple, isolated locations within each Region.
They are designed to be located far enough apart to significantly reduce the risk of a single event impacting multiple zones..
Definition: Azure : Availability Zones are unique physical locations within an Azure region, each made up of one or more datacenters equipped with independent power, cooling, and networking..
Definition: GCP : Google Cloud Platform's equivalent to Availability Zones is called zones.
They are physically isolated locations within a region that provide low-latency connectivity between them..
Number of Zones: AWS: There is no minimum number specified, but there are multiple isolated locations within each Region..
Number of Zones: Azure: A minimum of three separate zones is available in all enabled regions..
Number of Zones: GCP: The number of zones varies by region, with some regions having as few as 3 and others having up to 15 zones..
Fault Domain and Update Domain: Azure : An availability zone is a combination of a fault domain and an update domain.
If you create three or more VMs across three zones in an Azure region, your VMs are effectively distributed across three fault domains and three update domains..
Fault Domain and Update Domain: GCP : Google Cloud Platform does not explicitly mention the concept of fault and update domains for its zones..
Integration with Managed Disks: Azure : Managed disks support availability zones, which help protect your applications from datacenter failures..

Across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Availability Zones (AZs) serve as distinct physical locations within a region to increase fault tolerance and stability.
Definition: In AWS , an Availability Zone is a distinct location that's engineered to be isolated from other Availability Zones within the same region, ensuring maximum fault tolerance.
In Azure , an Availability Zone is a combination of a fault domain and an update domain, made up of one or more datacenters equipped with independent power, cooling, and networking.
In GCP , a zone refers to a physical location that's part of a region, providing isolated resources for increased fault tolerance..

Mapping: In AWS, the mapping of Availability Zone codes to AZ IDs is unique for each account to ensure resources are distributed across the Availability Zones for a Region .
In Azure, an Availability Zone is a combination of a fault domain and an update domain, which can help distribute VMs across three fault domains and three update domains .
GCP does not provide specific information about AZ mapping..

## Fargate Throttling Quotas (Token Bucket Algorithm)

AWS Fargate limits Amazon ECS tasks and Amazon EKS pods launch rates using a token bucket algorithm for each AWS account on a per-Region basis :

| Actions | Bucket maximum capacity (or Burst rate) | Bucket refill rate (or Sustained rate) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fargate Resource rate quota for On Demand Amazon ECS tasks and Amazon EKS pods | 100 | 20 |
| Fargate Resource rate quota for Spot Amazon ECS tasks | 100 | 20 |

Example: The tasks and pods token bucket size for a Fargate customer account is 100 tokens, and the refill rate is 20 tokens per second.

Therefore, you can immediately launch up to 100 Amazon ECS tasks and Amazon EKS pods per customer account, with a sustained launch rate of 20 Amazon ECS tasks and Amazon EKS pods per second

| PUT ManagedCluster | 20 requests | 1 request / 1 minute | ManagedCluster |
| GET ManagedCluster | 60 requests | 1 request / 1 second | Managed Cluster |
| GET Operation Status | 200 requests | 2 requests / 1 second | Subscription |
| All Other APIs | 60 requests | 1 request / 1 second | Subscription |

Reserved Instances have discount pricing tiers - When you buy Reserved Instances, Amazon EC2 automatically applies any discounts to the part of your purchase that falls within a discount pricing tier.
List value calculation - You can determine the pricing tier for your account by calculating the list value for all of your Reserved Instances in a Region.
The list value is calculated by: Multiplying the hourly recurring price for each reservation by the total number of hours for the term.
List value calculation - You can determine the pricing tier for your account by calculating the list value for all of your Reserved Instances in a Region.
The list value is calculated by: Adding the undiscounted upfront price (also known as the fixed price) at the time of purchase.
Four purchase scenarios - When buying Reserved Instances, one of four possible scenarios occurs: No discount - Your purchase within a Region is still below the discount threshold.

Four purchase scenarios - When buying Reserved Instances, one of four possible scenarios occurs: Partial discount - Your purchase crosses the threshold of the first discount tier; no discount is applied to one or more reservations and the discounted rate is applied to the remaining reservations.

Four purchase scenarios - When buying Reserved Instances, one of four possible scenarios occurs: Full discount - Your entire purchase within a Region falls within one discount tier and is discounted appropriately.

Four purchase scenarios - When buying Reserved Instances, one of four possible scenarios occurs: Two discount rates - Your purchase crosses from a lower discount tier to a higher discount tier; you are charged two different rates.

Tier crossing behavior - After the list value of your active Reserved Instances in a Region crosses into a discount pricing tier, any future purchase of Reserved Instances in that Region are charged at a discounted rate.
If a single purchase crosses the threshold, the portion above the price threshold is charged at the discounted rate.

# Comparative Answer: AWS VPC vs AWS IAM

## Use Cases

| Feature | AWS VPC | AWS IAM |
|---------|---------|---------|
| Primary Purpose | Network isolation and resource grouping within AWS | Secure access control and authentication for AWS resources |
| Access Control | Controls which VPC resources can be accessed via condition keys (e.g., [CODE]) | Controls who can be authenticated and authorized to use AWS resources |
| Resource Association | Associated with EC2 instances, route tables, and other AWS services | Associated with EC2 instances, ECS tasks, and other AWS services via roles |

## Features

| Feature | AWS VPC | AWS IAM |
|---------|---------|---------|
| Condition Keys | [CODE] - requires full ARN of the VPC to specify | [CODE] - global condition key usable across services |
| Pricing | Not specified in context | Free to use with no additional charge  |
| Service Integration | Works with EC2, route tables, and VPC resources | Works with EC2, ECS, and other AWS services |
| Configuration | Must specify full ARN of VPC for condition keys | Can be attached to instances via IAM roles or instance profiles |
| Virtualization Support | N/A | N/A (IAM is separate from virtualization types) |

## Key Differences.

Discount Pricing Tier Concept**.
When you buy Reserved Instances, Amazon EC2 automatically applies discounts to purchases that fall within a discount pricing tier.
After your list value of active Reserved Instances in a Region crosses into a discount pricing tier, future purchases are charged at a discounted rate.

Four Possible Discount Scenarios**
When purchasing Reserved Instances, one of four scenarios occurs:.
No discount – Purchase within a Region is still below the discount threshold.
Partial discount – Purchase crosses the threshold of the first discount tier; no discount applied to one or more reservations, discounted rate applied to remaining reservations.
Full discount – Entire purchase within a Region falls within one discount tier and is discounted appropriately.
Two discount rates – Purchase crosses from a lower discount tier to a higher discount tier; charged two different rates.
List value is based on undiscounted (public) pricing and is not affected by volume discounts or price drops after purchase.
Formula: Multiply hourly recurring price × total hours for term + undiscounted upfront price (fixed price).
Example: For a 1-year Partial Upfront [CODE] Reserved Instance with $60.00 upfront price and $0.007 hourly rate, list value = $121.32.
A consolidated billing account aggregates the list value of member accounts within a Region.
When list value reaches a discount pricing tier, Reserved Instances purchased after this point by any member are charged at the discounted rate.
